subject: Shiny: Reverse Proxy and websockets problem

messages.author: 57b77f027eedfedc
messages.subject: Shiny: Reverse Proxy and websockets problem
parts:
I'm developing an app (http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/) which was working fine until I put it under a reverse proxy (Shiny-server 0.4.0.15, using Apache2 2.4.7, Ubuntu 14.04 - as per the instructions for Rstudio/shiny).

When the app is loaded under a reverse proxy, Firefox's JS inspector returns

"GET http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/jdq4jk8b/websocket [HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request 32ms]
Firefox can't establish a connection to the server at ws://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/jdq4jk8b/websocket. [sockjs-0.3.min.js:27]"

The app continues to function ok (after selecting a stream and a site on the first tab, all of the controls on all of the tabs work fine), until you return to the first tab and attempt to select another stream.  At that point, the app grays out with the following message on the JS inspector.
"POST http://urbanstreams.net/tools/bugmodels/__sockjs__/017/f5ur9uwf/xhr_send [HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden 13ms]"

I see that others have had trouble with websockets and shiny with a reverse proxy (mostly from a year ago), but I haven't been able to find any reports of this problem.

Thanks!

Many thanks for your quick response Joe - Sorry for the long delay - I had to put this down for a few weeks - just getting back to it now.
The log files don't seem to be reporting anything other than the warnings and notifications I get when I run it (without error) without the reverse proxy.  
It grays out once it has rendered the ggmap plots - here are the warnings from the log file for that point

Warning: bounding box given to google - spatial extent only approximate.

converting bounding box to center/zoom specification. (experimental)

Map from URL :
http://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/staticmap?center=-37.769915,145.225646&zoom=13&size=%20640x640&scale=%202&maptype=hybrid&sensor=false

Google Maps API Terms of Service : http://developers.google.com/maps/terms

I should say that I have found that my "bugmodels" app works without a problem in Chrome, but crashes when used in Safari or Firefox.

I have a second app that plots a leaflet map
http://urbanstreams.net/tools/melbmap/
which I am intending to combine with my "bugmodels" app . It is also works fine when accessed directly through port 3838, but behind a reverse proxy it crashes (usually after clicking on a few points), giving similar JS 'websockets' errors to the ones I reported earlier.  And this app crashes in Chrome as well as Safari and Firefox.

I also note that the Shiny Superzip example is doing the same thing now.

A larger problem perhaps?
